spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶2:**
The reception of the divine calling and the confirmation of divine truth have their origin in the principal faculties of the heavenly order. They were distinguished thus: reception belongs to the Lord's invitation toward good, and confirmation belongs to the will's answering acknowledgment of that good. Together they form the complete circuit by which divine influx is both given and reciprocated.

**¶3:**
Just as the divine calling and the will's obedient response were the very openings through which states of divine compassion and humble supplication became accessible to the celestial mind in its captivity, so also these same openings served the divine sphere from which spiritual truths are born and the divine good from which all spiritual life proceeds. The celestial mind, in its state of bondage, sought liberation and found its deliverer. And likewise the generative sphere of truth and the originating good of life sought [GAP-1: to recover and draw back to themselves] this emanation of will that had gone forth from them — which is the celestial mind itself; but the divine calling and the responsive obedience of the will became the states of access through which this recovery was accomplished.

**¶4:**
In this manner, the calling and the response became openings through which the successive heavenly states of the divine order could reach the celestial mind, and could reach the spiritual life that had become conjoined with the death of evil and falsity. They became ministering agencies [GAP-2: and instruments of liberation] for the celestial mind during its elevation into interior spiritual states. They restored to it [GAP-3: the living connection with] the originating divine good and the generative sphere of divine truth [GAP-4: from whom it had been separated by its descent into darkness]. They are the purifying powers of the spiritual life within the person, being ministering agencies and restorers of interior recollection for that life, whether it dwells [GAP-5: in the state of interior perception, that is,] in the form of living knowledge, or in the state of embodiment in the natural and corporeal mind [GAP-6: where it has been enclosed and forgotten].

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The assent and the amen have come about from these great ones of the powers. They were given the name as the assent belongs to the summons and the amen belongs to the answer.

Just as the summons and the obedience are the ones that opened the portals of mercy and entreaty for the First Man, so they also became portals for the Mother of Life and the Father of the living. The First Man sought and found his redeemer. And also the Mother of Life and the Father of the living sought [and found] this runner, who came forth from them, who is the First Man; but the summons and the obedience became the portals for them.

Now, in this way they have become portals for the aeons of greatness towards the First Man, and the soul that was conjoined with death. They became helpers [and redeemers] of the First Man during his ascent. They gave him [back to] the Father of Life and the Mother of Life [from whom he was separated]. They are purifiers of the living soul, being helpers and bestowers of remembrance for it, be it either in [the fruit of] in the tree or in the creation of flesh [where it is bound and has forgotten]

fills.explanation: Creates deliberate parallelism with the preceding sentence ("The First Man sought and found his redeemer"), expressing the spiritual reality of recovery — the Mother and Father likewise sought and recovered this emanation that had gone forth from them.

The spiritual reading indicates "instruments of liberation," which in the Kephalaia's natural-plane register of Manichaean soteriology translates to "redeemers" — paired with "helpers" to form the standard doublet describing the agencies of the First Man's deliverance.

The spiritual reading says "restored to it the living connection with" the Father and Mother — in the Kephalaia's narrative register, the summons and obedience gave the First Man back to his divine parents, restoring the severed connection through his ascent.

The spiritual reading indicates "from whom it had been separated by its descent into darkness" — in Kephalaia register, this relative clause identifies the Father and Mother as the divine source from whom the First Man was parted through his descent into the battle with darkness.

The spiritual reading maps GAP-5 to "the state of interior perception, that is" linked appositively to the tree (= living knowledge); in the Kephalaia's natural-plane vocabulary, fruit corresponds to interior perception (the good perceived within knowledge), yielding the standard Manichaean pair "the fruit of the tree" parallel to "the creation of flesh."

fills.fill: where it is bound and has forgotten
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "where it has been enclosed and forgotten"; in Kephalaia register, the living soul in flesh is "bound" (enclosed/imprisoned) and "has forgotten" its origin — directly mirroring the text's reference to the summons and obedience as "bestowers of remembrance" for the soul that has forgotten.
